slides.title: Encryption
points: Encryption protects confidentiality by transforming readable plaintext into ciphertext using cryptographic keys and algorithms.
Security+ Objective 1.4: explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions.

breakdown.explanation: Everything on the drive is protected when the device is powered off and locked.

course.why: It protects data at rest if a laptop or drive is lost or stolen.
course.example: A stolen laptop's entire SSD remains unreadable without the key.
course.check_q: Which encryption level best protects an entire stolen laptop drive?

breakdown.explanation: Only one partition is encrypted, not necessarily the whole disk.

course.why: It can isolate protected data to a designated partition.
course.example: Only the finance partition on a multi-partition disk is encrypted.
course.check_q: Which level encrypts only one disk partition?

breakdown.explanation: Protection is applied to selected files rather than the whole disk.

course.why: It allows granular protection of specific sensitive files.
course.example: Only an HR spreadsheet is encrypted.
course.check_q: Which encryption level protects a single document?

breakdown.explanation: A logical volume is protected as a unit.

course.why: It provides storage-level protection for a defined volume.
course.example: A logical data volume mounted as a drive is encrypted.
course.check_q: Which level protects a logical storage volume?

slides.title: Database Encryption
slides.teach: Encrypts data stored in a database.

course.learn: Encrypts data stored in a database.

breakdown.explanation: The database or its stored contents are protected at rest.

course.why: It protects sensitive structured data if underlying storage is exposed.
course.example: Customer records in a production database are encrypted at rest.
course.check_q: Which level protects data stored in a database?

breakdown.explanation: Only specific records are encrypted instead of the entire database.

course.why: It provides more granular protection for selected sensitive data.
course.example: Only records containing regulated data are encrypted.
course.check_q: Which level protects selected database records?

slides.title: Transport / Communication Encryption
slides.teach: Protects data while it moves between systems.

course.learn: Protects data while it moves between systems.
course.why: It reduces the risk of interception or exposure across networks.
course.check_q: Which encryption protects data moving across a network?

slides.title: Symmetric Encryption
slides.teach: Uses the same shared secret key for encryption and decryption.

course.learn: Uses the same shared secret key for encryption and decryption.

breakdown.explanation: Both sides rely on one shared secret.

course.why: It is fast and efficient for bulk data encryption.
course.example: A backup archive is encrypted with AES.
course.check_q: Which type uses one shared secret key?

breakdown.explanation: One key can be shared and the other remains secret.

course.why: It supports key establishment, signatures, and trust without sharing the private key.
course.example: A public key is used during certificate-based communication.
course.check_q: Which type uses a public/private key pair?

slides.title: Key Exchange
slides.teach: A method for securely establishing or sharing cryptographic keys between parties.

course.learn: A method for securely establishing or sharing cryptographic keys between parties.

breakdown.explanation: It helps two parties agree on keying material.

course.why: Symmetric encryption needs a secure way to establish shared keys.
course.example: Two systems use ECDHE to derive shared session keys.
course.exam: Need to establish a shared key → KEY EXCHANGE.
course.check_q: What concept establishes cryptographic keys between parties?

slides.title: Algorithms
slides.teach: The mathematical procedures used to perform cryptographic operations.

course.learn: The mathematical procedures used to perform cryptographic operations.

breakdown.explanation: The algorithm defines how the cryptographic transformation works.

course.why: Appropriate algorithm selection affects security, compatibility, and performance.
course.example: An organization selects AES for bulk data encryption.
course.check_q: What determines the mathematical procedure used for encryption?

slides.title: Key Length
slides.teach: The size of a cryptographic key.

course.learn: The size of a cryptographic key.

breakdown.explanation: Key length is one factor affecting resistance to brute-force attacks.

course.why: Insufficient key length can weaken protection even when the algorithm is otherwise appropriate.
course.example: An organization chooses a stronger approved key size for a long-lived key.
course.check_q: What property describes the size of a cryptographic key?

blocks.title: Identify what is being protected and how
items: Protect the entire drive when physical theft is the concern.
Example: A stolen laptop remains unreadable without the key.
Use file-level protection when only selected files need encryption.
Example: A single HR spreadsheet is encrypted.
Protect data while it moves across a network.
A shared secret makes symmetric encryption efficient for large amounts of data.
Example: AES encrypts a backup archive.
Public/private keys support trust, signatures, and secure key establishment.
Example: A public key is used during certificate-based communication.
blocks.example: Memory: Whole device · One file · Data in transit · One shared secret · Key pair.

questions.q: A company wants a stolen laptop's entire drive to remain unreadable without authentication. Which solution best fits?
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption protects the entire storage device.

questions.q: Only one sensitive spreadsheet needs cryptographic protection. Which encryption level is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: File encryption protects selected files individually.

questions.q: A company needs to protect customer data while it travels between a browser and a web server. Which solution applies?
questions.explanation: Transport encryption protects data in transit.

questions.q: Which cryptographic approach uses one shared secret and is generally preferred for efficient bulk encryption?
questions.explanation: Symmetric encryption uses one shared secret and is efficient for bulk data.

questions.q: Which cryptographic approach uses a public key and a private key?
questions.explanation: Asymmetric encryption uses a public/private key pair.

questions.q: Two systems need to securely establish shared session keying material. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Key exchange establishes cryptographic keys between parties.

questions.q: A database protects only selected rows containing regulated information. Which encryption level is being used?
questions.explanation: Record encryption protects selected rows or records.

questions.q: A company encrypts an entire logical storage volume but not the rest of the physical disk. Which level is this?
questions.explanation: Volume encryption protects a logical volume.

questions.q: What cryptographic property refers to the size of a key, such as 128-bit or 256-bit?
questions.explanation: Key length is the size of the cryptographic key.

questions.q: Which term refers to the mathematical procedure used to perform cryptographic operations?
questions.explanation: The algorithm defines the mathematical cryptographic procedure.
